newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian oil, fuel rail tariffs due to fall-agency.
newsitem.headline: Russian oil, fuel rail tariffs due to fall-agency.

text.p: The costs of transporting oil and heavy fuel by rail in Russia are set to fall by 25 percent from July 1 this year in cases where the distance covered exceeds 2,500 km (1,600 miles), Interfax news agency quoted a spokesman for Fuel and Energy Minister Boris Nemtsov as saying on Friday.
He was also quoted as saying that rail tariffs on timber materials and coal would fall by 50 percent in cases where the distance covered exceeds 3,000 km (1,900 miles), he was quoted as saying.

Other rail tariff changes slated for July 1 include a 50 percent cut for building materials and for industrial-mineral raw materials, the spokesman said, without adding further details as to exactly what these categories included.
The spokesman also said that rail tariffs for sugar beets would be cut by 40 percent.
He was quoted as saying that the tariff reductions were made as a result of actions agreed between the Economy, Finance and Transport Ministries.
Nemtsov has been given the reponsibility of re-vamping the country's natural monpolies, including the sprawling railway system.

Railway tariffs can represent a major cost for crude oil and oil product producers in Russia, with oil fields and refineries often situated thousands of kilometres from vital hard currency markets in the west and even from domestic consumers.
